chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: First tour away from home at fourteen and the Trianon Ballroom
summary: His mother entrusted him to front man Ivan Rowe; at Fort Lauderdale's Trianon the Black band waited for white men to leave the toilet.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So after I was with this group for about six months, they decided that when school closed, we should go out on tour --this was my first time away from home. I was just 14, and Ivan [Rowe]was our front man; he was the front man for our band -- and my mother asked him to take care of me while we were away.

Well, we used to play every Saturday night at a dance hall up at Ft. Lauderdale called the Trianon Ballroom, and the Trianon Ballroom -- we used to have to play until intermission, and then we would line up and they would tell all of the white men to come out of the men's room, so we could go in and we would all line up and go into the men's room there, and relieve ourselves and then go back and sit back up on the bandstand.
